title: How to Clean Messy Data in Excel With AI (Fast & Free)
short_title: Clean messy Excel data in seconds
description:
Messy spreadsheets waste hours. In this video a free AI chatbot helps you fix the most common data problems in Excel and Google Sheets:

- Find what's wrong with your data
- Remove extra spaces (TRIM)
- Fix random capitals (PROPER)
- Clean phone numbers (SUBSTITUTE)
- Remove duplicates
- Join or split names
- Count empty cells (COUNTBLANK)
- Google Sheets one-click cleanup

Works with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or any free AI chatbot.

Subscribe to Work Hacked for a new work shortcut every week.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#excel #datacleaning #AItools

scenes.narration: Messy spreadsheets waste hours. Extra spaces, random capitals, duplicates, broken phone numbers. Today AI fixes all of it in minutes, and I'll show you exactly how.
Step zero, and don't skip it. Make a copy of your file first, so you can always go back.

screen.title: Before you start
items: Make a copy of your file

scenes.narration: Start by pasting five or six messy rows into an AI chatbot, and ask it what's wrong with your data. It spots problems you might miss.

screen.user: Here are 5 rows from my customer list: [paste]. What's wrong with this data, and how do I fix each problem in Excel?
screen.ai: 1. Extra spaces in names. 2. Mixed capital letters. 3. Duplicate customers. 4. Phone numbers have dashes.

scenes.narration: Problem one. Extra spaces. They're invisible, but they break lookups and sorting. One formula removes them.
Problem two. Random capital letters. Wrap it in PROPER, and every name looks neat.
Problem three. Phone numbers full of dashes. Ask AI to remove them, and you get one clean format.
Problem four. Duplicates. You don't even need a formula. In Excel, go to Data, then Remove Duplicates. In Google Sheets, it's Data, Data cleanup, Remove duplicates.
Problem five. First and last names stuck in one cell, or split when you need them together. AI gives you both fixes.

screen.user: First names are in A and last names in B. How do I join them into one cell with a space?

scenes.narration: Drag it down, and the full names fill in for every row.
Need the opposite? To split one column into two, use Text to Columns in Excel, or Split text to columns in Google Sheets.

screen.title: Split one column into two
items: Sheets: Data, Split text to columns

scenes.narration: Problem six. Empty cells. Ask AI for a quick count, so you know how much data is missing.
Google Sheets users get a bonus. Under Data, Data cleanup, there's Cleanup suggestions and Trim whitespace, which fix common problems in one click.
Last step. Once your clean columns look right, copy them and paste as values, so they stay fixed even if you delete the messy ones.
So, ask AI what's wrong, fix spaces, capitals, phone numbers and duplicates, join or split names, and check for blanks. Your data is ready.
